channel.title: Curated Engineering Reads
channel.description: A weekly hand-picked selection of engineering and data science blog posts on experimentation, forecasting, analytics engineering, and AI agents for data work.

item.title: How we built a personal data scientist for every Notion employee
item.description:
An internal analytics assistant grounded in governed Snowflake tables plus the company's own written context, rather than in the warehouse alone. The pairing is the transferable part: a data agent needs the curated layer and the docs that define it, or it answers confidently from tables nobody agreed on.
Source: Notion Blog

item.title: How Notion built a Custom Agent workflow to keep Academy content current
item.description:
An agent spots content gaps, drafts the fix, and only approved drafts get written back to the live platform. That propose-then-approve shape is the one to copy for keeping data model documentation current: the agent does the detection and drafting, a human gate stands between it and anything that ships.
Source: Notion Blog

item.title: Metrics Board: Building an Agent-ready Metrics Layer
item.description:
Metric quality and ownership are enforced when a metric is created rather than audited later, which is the thing that makes the same definitions safe for an agent to query instead of letting it loose on raw tables. Worth reading as a design for your own metric layer: the intake checks and the producer-ownership model are the transferable parts, not the petabyte scale.
Source: Pinterest Engineering

item.title: ShopGym: Realistic, reproducible sandboxes for shopping agents
item.description:
A generated store plus generated tasks gives every agent run the same fixed environment, so a change to the agent can be measured rather than demoed. The same shape applies to your data agents: a frozen snapshot of the warehouse and a generated question set turn text-to-SQL or triage evaluation into a repeatable regression test.
Source: Shopify Engineering

item.title: A problem well-defined is half solved: Measuring Hypothesis Quality at Booking.com
item.description:
Booking makes the hypothesis itself the quality gate: the evidence behind the idea, the user response expected, and the decision criteria all written down before launch, then scored. That is a rubric you can drop into your own experiment intake so a clear result arrives already attached to a decision instead of a debate.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: Why Spotify Is Not Using Bayesian A/B Testing
item.description:
A team that runs experimentation at scale explaining why it stayed frequentist and what the Bayesian label does and does not actually change. Read it before your team spends a quarter evaluating a switch, and keep it for the next time someone asks why you haven't.
Source: Spotify Engineering

item.title: When Can LLMs Replace Humans in A/B Tests?
item.description:
The useful part is the framing: LLM-predicted outcomes substitute for human ones only under assumptions you have to state and defend, not as a free measurement upgrade. Directly relevant if you are tempted to let a judge model stand in for a real metric in a test.
Source: Spotify Engineering

item.title: From weeks to a day: how we made LLM evaluation fast enough to iterate on
item.description:
Airbnb's cut from weeks to a day came from ordinary engineering on the eval harness - caching, determinism, handling judges that disagree with themselves - not from better models. The layered breakdown is a good checklist for why your own agent evals are too slow to iterate on.
Source: Airbnb Tech Blog

item.title: Blueberry: Force Multiplier For The On-Call Engineer
item.description:
A Slack-native reasoning harness aimed at the worst minutes of an incident, when nobody yet agrees what is broken, and at turning tribal knowledge into context the agent can reuse. Close to the operational triage work you are building, and concrete about where the harness boundary sits.
Source: Instacart Tech

item.title: The Causality Gap: Measuring the True Impact of Voluntary Adoption in Digital Marketplaces
item.description:
For opt-in features, a flat A/B topline can hide a strong product behind low adoption. Randomized encouragement plus DoubleML separates the effect on adopters (ATT) from the rollout effect (ITT), and the gap tells you whether to fix the product or the adoption funnel.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: Scaling Experimentation Quality at Booking.com
item.description:
A three-pillar quality metric (design, execution, decision) tracked per experiment, plus the finding that strong tool defaults beat enforcement. Useful template for how a working group measures and raises experiment quality.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: Outlier Handling at Scale in Experimentation
item.description:
Use A/A permutation tests to detect metrics that heavy tails are breaking, then winsorize. Includes a practical heuristic for picking the cap and a max-to-99.9th-percentile ratio as a quick warning sign.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: A Recap of the 2026 Experimentation Conference at Booking.com
item.description:
Two ideas worth taking: Deliveroo builds its testing standards into the tooling (locked primary metrics, mandatory guardrails), and Booking's micro-conversions cut runtime from 34 to 14 days while keeping the business metric as a guardrail.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: How we knew COVID was over (and what our models had to unlearn)
item.description:
A decision rule for drifting forecasts: refit, respecify, or hold. Misses that stay one-sided point to a structural problem a refit can't fix. Directly applicable to running a demand forecast in production.
Source: Airbnb Tech Blog

item.title: Predicting Rider Conversion in Sparse Data Environments with Bayesian Trees
item.description:
A hierarchy of small models where each child is pulled toward its parent's parameters when it has little data. The same pattern fits forecasting down to thin segments without overfitting.
Source: Lyft Engineering

item.title: Metric Semantic Layer: How Lyft Governs and Scales Key Data Definitions
item.description:
Metric definitions as YAML plus Jinja SQL, admitted only with two or more real use cases, each owned by a business team and a data team. The MCP layer on top lets AI tools answer from the same governed definitions. Maps onto the gold layer and Sigma.
Source: Lyft Engineering

item.title: Modeling Device Capabilities for Analytics
item.description:
A short gold-layer pattern: a cumulative latest-state table paired with a 28-day histogram table for distribution questions.
Source: Netflix TechBlog

item.title: Partition Finalization in Pinterest's Next-Generation DB Ingestion Framework
item.description:
Answers 'when is a streaming partition complete enough to read?' with an event-time watermark stored in Iceberg table metadata. A good model for gating downstream gold jobs on streaming sources.
Source: Pinterest Engineering

item.title: Eval-driven development: Lessons from evaluating GenAI at scale
item.description:
A practical eval playbook: read outputs first, build a 50 to 100 example golden set with bad examples, keep 3 to 5 calibrated LLM judges, and evaluate agent trajectories, not only final answers.
Source: Airbnb Tech Blog

item.title: Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement
item.description:
Argues the methodology belongs in the harness around the model, so analysis is reproducible and auditable. Close to how an agent workforce for data work should be framed.
Source: Airbnb Tech Blog

item.title: From Traditional ML to AI Agents: How Booking.com Scales AI Observability With Arize AI
item.description:
Two telemetry paths, OpenTelemetry traces for agents and warehouse logs for classic ML, into one observability platform. Relevant to tracing a job-failure triage agent.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: AI Agent Evaluation
item.description:
Black-box versus glass-box agent evaluation, with task completion scored by an LLM judge as the headline metric.
Source: Booking.com ML & DS

item.title: Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model
item.description:
How to design agent infrastructure so it survives model upgrades rather than being rebuilt around each one.
Source: Shopify Engineering

item.title: Becoming an AI Team
item.description:
A manager's view of moving to an AI-first operating model: the capacity tipping point and how the manager role shifts toward strategy. Worth sharing with the team.
Source: Pinterest Engineering

item.title: From Day 1 to Production: Building Lyft's Analytics & Rides Intelligence Assistant
item.description:
A natural-language analytics assistant going from Streamlit prototype to production service. Skim it if the data agents need a proper front end.
Source: Lyft Engineering
